title: prompt-library-scratchpad-samira
content:
Quick scratchpad for prompt templates / few-shot sets / failure cases. Mostly notes-to-self and rough experiments.

Goals:
- Build small, reusable templates for customer-facing retrieval-augmented responses and product copy generation.
- Capture failure modes and concrete mitigations (e.g., prompt truncation, few-shot ordering, instruction ambiguity).
- Keep a canonical few-shot for each vertical (support replies, marketing blurbs, FAQ answer, code explain).

Notes / context:
- Using open models (Llama-2 style) and a couple of internal Redwood-verified checkpoints. Need to test across seq-len 512/2048.
- Prior experiments (see GH PR above) show model is sensitive to shot order and to trailing punctuation in instructions.
- TODO: add automated eval harness (microbench vs. small eval set) and link results here.

Template: RAG short-answer (concise, cite source)
- Instruction: "You are an assistant that answers concisely using the provided context. Always cite the source by id in square brackets after the sentence that uses it. If the answer is not contained in the context, say \"I don't know\". Keep answer <= 3 sentences."
- Input fields: [CONTEXT], [QUESTION]
- Postprocess: Strip aggressive hedging, prefer active voice.

Few-shot example set (3 shots) => Support reply (ticket-summarization style)

Shot 1:
CONTEXT: [doc: KB-001] The feature toggles are controlled via /api/toggles. To enable, send POST with {\"name\":..., \"enabled\":true}.
QUESTION: "How do I enable the new billing toggle for my org?"
ANSWER: "Call POST /api/toggles with JSON {\"name\": \"billing_new_ui\", \"enabled\": true}. If you use the CLI, run: redwood toggle set billing_new_ui --on [KB-001]"

Shot 2:
CONTEXT: [doc: KB-042] Only org admins can change billing preferences. There is a UI flow under Settings > Billing.
QUESTION: "Can non-admins enable the toggle?"
ANSWER: "No. Only org admins can change billing toggles; direct them to Settings > Billing or provide an admin to perform the POST. [KB-042]"

Shot 3:
CONTEXT: [doc: KB-803] Toggle changes may take up to 30s to propagate to edge caches. CI jobs should retry once on 429-like errors.
QUESTION: "Will this take effect immediately?"
ANSWER: "It can take up to 30s to propagate; design your clients to retry once on transient errors. [KB-803]"

Notes: keep context fragments short (<=125 tokens). Shots ordered from general to specific reduced repetition helps with model focus.

Failure cases observed:
- Hallucinated endpoints: when context is long and the instruction vague, model invents endpoint names (fix: anchor to explicit code examples in context, add examples in few-shots that show exact JSON).
- Truncation sensitivity: if context plus shots exceed model window, model tends to ignore later docs - solution: prioritized context ranking and reduce shots to 1-2 plus a short instruction.
- Temperature drift: using temp 0.0 reduces creativity but sometimes leads to terse/incomplete answers - experiment with 0.05-0.2 for balance.
- Citation loss: model sometimes omits the square-bracket id; mitigate by requiring a final line: "Sources: [ids]" as a strict template.

Quick experiments (results inline):
- Exp A: 3-shot RAG vs 1-shot + rerank; model prefers 1-shot + rerank when context size >1200 tokens (qual rating: 4/5 usefulness).
- Exp B: Add explicit end-of-context token "<END_CONTEXT>" improves citation placement by ~30% (manual check on 50 examples).
- Exp C: Swap shot order (specific->general) leads to more terse answers but sometimes better error handling. Keep both variants for A/B.

Short templates to add to library:
- "support_short_answer": instruction + 1 shot, fallback phrase.
- "marketing_blurb": instruction that enforces tone (cheerful, 1 paragraph, <= 60 words). Include few-shot with 2 examples.
- "code_explain": provide snippet + ask for line-by-line explanation, prefer bullet output, limit tokens.

Example marketing_blurb few-shot (2 examples)
Shot1 Input: "Product: Redwood Inference; Feature: Dedicated capacity; Tone: confident, punchy"
Output: "Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU power and predictable latency so your product never stalls - simple contracts, enterprise-grade SLAs, and hands-off scaling."

Shot2 Input: "Product: Redwood Optimize; Feature: intelligent batching; Tone: helpful, concise"
Output: "Cut per-token costs without sacrificing latency using workload-aware batching and smart cache policies - automatically tuned to your traffic patterns."

Evaluation heuristics (manual + automated):
- Precision: does generated answer match context? (binary per example)
- Conciseness: <=3 sentences for support_short_answer
- Citation correctness: source id present and correct
- Tone match: manual 1-5 scale for marketing_blurb

Planned next steps:
- Add a 100-example eval set for each template and run nightly on hosted API (small subset of customers). Link results in Confluence.
- Implement strict post-processing: enforce citation presence and final "Sources:" line.
- Automate context selection: clip to top-K by BM25 + similarity, tune K per model/window.
- Save canonical few-shot sets in repo (repro-prompts) and add test harness.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we prefer 1-shot + rerank for long contexts (cost tradeoff)? Pros: smaller prompt per call, cons: extra roundtrip. Need cost vs quality numbers.
- How to version few-shots (shot-level metadata)? Propose naming: {template}-{version}-{model} e.g. support_short_answer-v2-llama2-13b.
- What is the best enforcement for citations? Model-level (instruction) or postprocess guardrails?

Scratch notes / random observations:
- When prompting for code explain, adding "Assume reader knows JS basics" reduces verbosity.
- Using example outputs that include the exact formatting we want (e.g., "Sources: [KB-001]") helps formatting consistency.
- Keep a short list of banned phrases for product copy (e.g., "best in class" - flagged by legal).

Record of quick runs (timestamps are local):
- 2026-01-12 09:23 run: 3-shot RAG (llama2-13b-q) -> mean citation presence 62% (50 ex).
- 2026-01-20 14:11 run: 1-shot + rerank (llama2-13b-q) -> mean citation presence 88% (50 ex).
- 2026-02-02 11:02 run: 1-shot + rerank + <END_CONTEXT> -> citation 94% (50 ex), slight drop in conciseness (more hedging).

References to add to canonical doc later:
- Confluence page: Prompt Library Home (link above).
- GH: repro-prompts PR 87 (contains eval harness).
- Linear ticket: RED-1234 for nightly eval infra.

End of scratchpad.
